docs.creator: Matthews, Hart, 1967-
description: Provides information about the first pilots from a hundred countries. A brief biography and a description of his or her attempts to fly are provided for each early aviator (except in a very few cases where facts are hard to find)

Most people recognize the Wright Brothers as the first in flight--in 1903, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. But few know that the next aviator, a Brazilian, flew almost three years later and was nevertheless widely credited as being the first in flight. Or that a world-famous Hungarian escapologist made the first flights in Australia, then never flew again. Or that in Spain the first public display of a flying machine led to religious riots. This book provides information about the first pilots from a hundred countries. A brief biography and a description of his or her attempts to fly are provided for each early aviator (except in a very few cases where facts are hard to find). A "flight" is defined as that made by a "heavier-than-air machine capable of taking off from ground level carrying a pilot, who controls to some degree the ascent, descent and path of the machine."--Back cover
docs.title: Pioneer aviators of the world : a biographical dictionary of the first pilots of 100 countries
